passages.context: Printed p. 159 was read at the page image. It carries canons III to IX in Waterworth's English, including canon VI, 'If anyone saith that the canon of the mass contains errors, and is therefore to be abrogated; let him be anathema', and canon IX, 'If anyone saith that the rite of the Roman Church, according to which a part of the canon and the words of consecration are pronounced in a low tone, is to be condemned; or that the mass ought to be celebrated in the vulgar tongue only; or that water ought not to be mixed with the wine that is to be offered in the chalice, for that it is contrary to the institution of Christ; let him be anathema.'

passages.context: Printed p. 156 was read at the page image. Waterworth's English of chapter IV, On the Canon of the Mass, closes: 'the Catholic Church instituted, many years ago, the sacred canon, so pure from every error, that nothing is contained therein which does not in the highest degree savour of a certain holiness and piety, and raise up unto God the minds of those that offer. For it is composed out of the very words of the Lord, the traditions of the Apostles, and the pious institutions also of holy pontiffs.' Chapter V, On the solemn ceremonies of the Sacrifice of the Mass, follows complete: 'therefore has holy Mother Church instituted certain rites, to wit, that certain things be pronounced in the mass in a low and others in a louder tone.'

work.author: Council of Trent
work.description: The canons and decrees of the ecumenical Council of Trent (1545-1563). Session XXIV of 11 November 1563 contains the canons on the sacrament of matrimony, of which canon 9 anathematizes the assertion that clerics in sacred orders or solemnly professed regulars can validly contract marriage notwithstanding the ecclesiastical law or vow, and canon 10 the assertion that the married state is to be preferred to virginity or celibacy.
work.title: Canones et decreta Concilii Tridentini
